_about: Night-sound candidates for design/night-sounds.html. Each file: a 32 s (crossfaded, seamless) loop cut from the Freesound HQ preview MP3, high-passed at 60 Hz, levelled to -30 LUFS integrated, peak-limited at -6 dBFS, AAC 96 kbps. All sources are CC0 1.0 (public domain dedication).

dawn-1.m4a.author: richwise

dawn-1.m4a.board_note: Hampshire countryside just before sunrise, a freezing April morning, far from roads. Scattered songbirds over a low rumble (the recordist mentions distant aircraft); bursts at 0:08 and 0:24.

dawn-2.m4a.board_note: Swiss mountain forest before sunrise: birds slowly waking, a little wind, a river far off. The sparsest and quietest: a few calls (0:02, 0:10, 0:18) over a soft wash.

snow-1.m4a.title: Quiet Winter Night with Light Snow & Wind – Altenthann Ambience - 260215_001
snow-1.m4a.author: TSP-Talk
snow-1.m4a.recordist_description: Altenthann – Winter Night Roomtone with Light Snowfall & Occasional Wind (15 February 2026, ~23:00) 48 kHz • 32‑bit float (HPF + gain adjust) • Omni Stereo (no Jecklin disc) This recording captures a cold winter night ambience in Altenthann, a quiet rural village in the district of Regensburg, Germany. Recorded late in the evening around 23:00 on 15 February 2026, the session documents a restrained and atmospheric interior–exterior hybrid roomtone with an open‑window perspective. Throughout the take, a very light, delicate snowfall can be heard settling onto nearby surfaces. As the recording progresses, the snowfall gradually increases in presence, adding a soft, granular texture that blends naturally into the quiet nighttime environment. The ambience features minimal distant traffic, characteristic of a remote rural community at night. Subtle wind gusts rise intermittently, creating gentle movements around the house structure and contributing to the depth of the winter soundscape. These wind surges add dynamic foley‑useful texture suitable for environmental layering or as transitional accents. The recording maintains a stable and low‑noise interior roomtone framing the external winter conditions. With omnidirectional microphones (no Jecklin disc), the stereo field is open, symmetrical, and diffuse — ideal for Foley, ambience beds, and post‑production layering, where natural width without enforced spatial separation is desired. Aside from a light high‑pass filter to remove sub‑bass rumble and careful gain adjustment, the recording remains raw and unprocessed, preserving the authenticity and subtlety expected in archival‑quality environmental audio. This ambience is particularly well‑suited for: night exterior / interior hybrid atmospheres winter environment transitions snowfall Foley layers quiet rural night scenes cinematic cold‑weather beds slow‑paced documentary environments ⚙️ Technical Specs Recording Date: 15 February 2026 (~23:00) Location: Altenthann (93177), Landkreis Regensburg, Bavaria, Germany Recorder: Zoom F3 Mics: Earsight The One (omni) Stereo Setup: Dual mono omni (no Jecklin disc) Format: 48 kHz • 32‑bit float → gain adjusted + gentle HPF Category: Ambience / Foley / Roomtone / Weather Key Elements: cold winter night ambience open‑window roomtone very light → increasing snowfall distant, minimal traffic intermittent wind gusts quiet rural nighttime atmosphere
snow-1.m4a.board_note: A winter night in a Bavarian village at 23:00, light snow, open window. Low and muffled with a faint village rumble; the calm stretch before the snow picks up.
